newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC to brief at 0600 GMT on global telecoms order.
newsitem.headline: NEC to brief at 0600 GMT on global telecoms order.

text.p: NEC Corp is expected to announce on Monday details of a contract it won last year from ICO Global Communications for a global mobile satellite communications service that is to start in 1999.
NEC will hold a news conference at 3 p.m. (0600 GMT) on an order for a global mobile satellite communications network. It has refused to disclose details of the news conference.
Last May, NEC, together with Hughes Network Systems of the United States and Swedish telecoms group Ericsson won a $500 million order to supply a communications system to ICO.
The ground system they will supply will be used to connect user terminals with wired or wireless telephones across the globe.
The system will be made up of 12 satellite access nodes (SANs), a network management centre and facilities to link the SANs and connect them to public switched networks.
ICO said at the time that it might place another $150 million order with the group led by NEC in order to meet demand up to 2010.

ICO was set up by 47 investors worldwide to develop the International Mobile Satellite Organisation's (Inmarsat) satellite-based mobile telephone system. Inmarsat is a multinational cooperative based in London.
NEC said in May it would become ICO's strategic partner through an equity investment in the company.
